title: Define runtime metadata and fallback triggers for unpinned open-model onboarding
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Clarify the minimal runtime metadata that must accompany new open-model submissions and specify automatic fallback triggers for unpinned variants. This ticket captures product requirements for model intake annotations (e.g., kv-cache-behavior, max-context, known-incompatibilities), the semantics of 'unpin' on the catalog, and the set of runtime signals that cause automatic pinning or fallback to a compatible variant at request time.
scope_changes: Initial intake required only lightweight metadata (format, size). Scope expanded to require: (1) explicit kv-cache compatibility tag, (2) expected latency bucket for 2k/8k contexts, (3) a runtime compatibility vector with required fences for kernels (FP32/INT8), and (4) fallback mapping rules for unpinned variants. These additions were approved by PM ↔ Runtime eng on 2026-03-05.
requirements: Intake schema: incoming model entries must include fields: model_id, variant_id, expected_max_sequence, quantization_support (enum), kv_cache_behavior (enum: full|partial|none), soft_compat_tags (list), provenance_url
Define 'unpinned' semantics: unpinned variant is allowed in catalog but runtime may select a pinned fallback if compatibility signals mismatch or SLAs would be violated

Runtime signals that trigger fallback: kernel incompatibility, OOM risk (>80% of observed batch memory), slow-path kernel selection causing estimated latency > SLO threshold, missing kv_cache support for features requiring prefix caching

Policy: automatic pinning in serving layer when variant demonstrates repeated graceful degradation (>=3 user requests with quality regression alerts within 24h) or when customer-configured safety flag is set
Rollout: catalog UI and API should surface unpinned indicator, expected_compatibility_score, and recommended pinned_fallbacks
Backwards compatibility: existing pinned models unaffected; adding these requirements must not invalidate historical entries — adopt soft fields with default 'unknown'
acceptance_criteria: Intake API accepts the new runtime metadata fields and validates types; server-side schema returns 400 on malformed enumerations
Catalog UI displays unpinned badge and links to fallback variants for every model without a pin
Serving runtime publishes decision logs when a fallback is chosen (model_requested -> model_served + reason). Logs visible in Console tracing for 30 days
E2E test demonstrating fallback triggered due to kv_cache mismatch and request served by recommended pinned variant within latency SLO
Rollout doc and PRD reviewed and approved by Runtime Eng, ML Infra, and Security teams
Migration plan documented for older catalog entries and a script to backfill 'kv_cache_behavior' as 'unknown' where missing
risks: False positives in fallback triggers could cause higher cost if runtime favors pinned high-cost variants unnecessarily
Incomplete metadata from community contributors increases runtime conservatism, risking degraded availability for new models
Ambiguous semantics around 'soft_compat_tags' may lead to inconsistent kernel selection across regions
Logging decision payloads could contain sensitive identifiers — must ensure PII-free traces or redaction
rollout_plan: Phase 1: API + schema change behind feature flag; allow submitters to include optional runtime fields (2 weeks). Phase 2: Console surfacing and decision-log plumbing (2 weeks). Phase 3: Enable conservative fallback logic in staging (1 week) and run a canary for selected tenants (2 weeks). Post-canary: enable catalog-visible unpinned badges globally and start auto-pinning rules if canary metrics meet cost/latency guardrails.
open_questions: How do we compute 'expected_compatibility_score' from sparse metadata? (score heuristics owned by Runtime Eng)
Should auto-pinning be reversible by tenant preference? (PM decision needed)
What thresholds for 'OOM risk' estimation are acceptable across GPU SKUs? (ops + runtime to propose)
Do we need to surface 'soft_compat_tags' to customers in the API, or only to internal routing logic?
